claims.claim: PARTLY SOURCED, PARTLY REMOVED: the article defined "held at the desk" in its own voice and added that it is "often a placeholder while the two chambers work toward a single, reconciled version." claims.claim: CORRECTED: the article said Wicker "pressed to bring it to the floor ahead of a bipartisan amendments agreement that cleared the way for passage." The sequence is the other way round. Roll Call records that the bill had been stalled since early September, that Wicker announced the agreed amendments package on the morning of October 9, and that the votes followed the same day. claims.claim: REMOVED: "Using an available bill as the vehicle for a negotiated final text is a common end-stage maneuver" was an unsourced frequency claim. No authority read for this audit supports it. CRS IF10516 makes the opposite-direction point - that the NDAA is used as a vehicle FOR other legislation - and using it here would have been a subtle misuse. Deleted and replaced with the sourced record of what S. 1071 actually was and how the House used it.

claims.claim: CORRECTED - NOT ON THE SWEEP LIST: the article said the December vote "drew the same 77-20 division" and, earlier in the same section, that the Senate agreed "by an identical 77-20 tally." The tally is identical; the division is not. Four senators changed sides - Baldwin (D-WI) and Durbin (D-IL) from no to yes, Bennet (D-CO) and Lee (R-UT) from yes to no - so the December bloc is 17 Democrats, one independent and TWO Republicans, not 18/1/1. claims.claim: ADDED - THE B1 LESSON APPLIED: the "What the FY2026 NDAA Authorizes" section was written entirely from the official summary, and that summary is of the bill AS REPORTED on 2025-07-15. The Senate passed S. 2296 with an amendment on 2025-10-09, and the engrossed text runs to TEN divisions - the four the summary describes plus Additional Provisions, the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Department of State Matters, the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, the ROAD to Housing Act and a Department of State Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026. A reader was being shown a four-division bill.
claims.sourceSpan: (9) Division I--ROAD to Housing Act.
claims.note: B1 established that a summary-derived section inherits the summary gaps. This case adds a second axis: the summary was also a VERSION behind, which is worse, because the gap is not an editorial choice by CRS but a bill that changed after the summary was written.

claims.claim: ADDED - NOT ON THE SWEEP LIST: the article described the DEI provisions only as the Senate bill repeals, and never told readers what the enacted law does. Section 901 of Public Law 119-60 is headed PROHIBITION OF DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION PROGRAMS and, beyond the same repeals, forward-bars a DEI office, a chief diversity officer, DEI plans and surveys, employee resource and affinity groups and DEI or critical-theory training, with a rule of construction preserving EEO and ADA offices. The two texts also differ structurally: ten divisions against eight, and the ROAD to Housing Act is in the Senate bill and nowhere in the law.
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 901. PROHIBITION OF DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION PROGRAMS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE.

claims.claim: CORRECTED, the only finding of the round-2 hostile source pass: the article read Wicker "announced that Republicans and Democrats had agreed on an amendments package" -- Roll Call reporter third-person narration, inside quotation marks, with Wicker as grammatical subject, two clauses away from a real Wicker quotation. A reader could not tell where the reporter stopped and the senator started. The quotation marks are gone and the fact is attributed to Roll Call. The underlying fact was never in doubt.

claims.note: Exactly the class the KOSA retrofit found (a press office third-person lead-in presented as the senators own words) and the class the emergency strike found on this very page (a headline word presented as something Markey said). Three instances now, in three different source types: press office, newspaper, headline. No scripted gate can catch it -- the phrase IS in the right file, attributed to the right subject; only the speaker boundary is wrong.

claims.claim: PROCESS NOTE, raised by the round-2 hostile verifier itself: the draft was being edited while that reviewer was reading it, and it caught the file mid-change twice. claims.note: Worth banking for the lane: applying fixes while a verifier is mid-read can produce findings against text that no longer exists, or hide text that does. Freeze the draft for the sign-off round.
